conceptual assets.information: The software-controlled enable determines whether the LED transmitter and its clock-generator request operate; disabling it also clears queued transmit data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: a bus write changes the stored enable at line 130, so an unauthorized write can alter operation. Availability: the enable directly drives clkgen_en_o at line 160 and clears the FIFO and controls engine state at lines 193 and 231, so changing it can disable or discard operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write can clear the enable, disable the clock-generator request, and discard queued LED transfers.

conceptual assets.concept: LED transfer format and strobe controls
conceptual assets.information: The mode and strobe settings select the serialized transfer format and the follow-on transmission behavior for queued LED words.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: bus writes store the mode and strobe settings at lines 131-132, and the serial engine uses them to select bit length and state at lines 240-251, so unauthorized modification can produce an incorrect LED waveform.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized control-register write can change the mode or strobe attribute of subsequent LED transfers and make the output format incorrect.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler and total, zero-bit, and one-bit timing settings determine the rate and pulse widths of serialized LED output, on which correct LED communication depends.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: bus writes store the timing settings at lines 133 and 135-137, and the serial engine uses them at lines 225, 261-263, 285, and 295, so unauthorized modification can corrupt waveform timing. Availability: the prescaler selects the sampled clock at line 225 and the timing comparisons advance or hold transmission at lines 278-299, so a malicious setting can stall or withhold serial output.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized write can select an unsuitable clock-generator bit or timing values, causing malformed pulses or a stalled LED transfer.

conceptual assets.information: The 32-bit payload received in a transmit bus write is queued and serialized onto neoled_o; LED output content depends on this payload.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: bus write data enters the transmit word at line 192 and is loaded and shifted for serial output at lines 239 and 257-270, so unauthorized modification can change displayed data. Availability: the enable-controlled FIFO clear at line 193 and the transmit-state decisions at lines 247 and 266-271 can discard or withhold a queued payload.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus write or disable operation can corrupt, discard, or prevent transmission of a queued LED payload.

conceptual assets.information: The internally generated interrupt request reports transmitter service conditions to the integrating system; servicing this request can be needed to keep queued LED transfers moving.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: irq_o is generated from the enable, interrupt selection, and FIFO conditions at lines 201-203, so those influences can cause a false or missing service request. Availability: suppressing the request at lines 201-203 can prevent the system from servicing the transmitter and leave transfers unprocessed.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized control or state change can suppress or forge irq_o, preventing required transmitter service or causing incorrect service.
